claimStartsWith: Public integrations require Notion review for users to add the app
quote: You can create and use a public connection without listing it.
note: Also tested: our OAuth connection's authorization URL worked immediately, with no review.

claimStartsWith: Notion requires HTTPS for all redirect URIs.
quote: We registered http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback and Notion accepted it.
note: The page says HTTPS, but http://localhost was accepted when we registered it.

claimStartsWith: Public distribution review by Notion takes 1 to 3 weeks.
quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.
note: Notion states 5 to 10 business days, which is shorter than the claimed range.

claimStartsWith: Public integrations must use OAuth tied to individual users
quote: OAuth: "User-scoped OAuth 2.0, with access limited to the signed-in user. Supports multiple workspaces and is Marketplace-eligible."

claimStartsWith: GitHub does not manually review or approve public OAuth or GitHub Apps
quote: Registering needed one form submission. GitHub showed no review step, no CAPTCHA, no password re-prompt and no email confirmation.
note: True for registering an OAuth app. We did not test Marketplace listing or a public GitHub App.

claimStartsWith: Public apps require hosting a Privacy Policy URL
quote: Filled four fields through the page's form controls: application name, homepage URL, description, one redirect URI.
note: A homepage URL is required, but the registration form never asked for a privacy policy.

claimStartsWith: Apps using restricted scopes require 1 to 4 weeks for approval
quote: Apps requesting access to restricted scopes must meet the additional requirement of secure data handling by submitting to an annual security assessment from a Google empanelled group of security assessors.
note: The assessment requirement is confirmed. No timeline is stated for restricted scopes.

claimStartsWith: Basic Sign-In OpenID Connect approval takes instant to a few hours.
quote: Open Permissions are the only permissions that are available to all developers without special approval.
note: These open permissions need no approval at all, so there is no approval time.
